references.title: CPF Act 1953 First Schedule — a bonus is an Additional Wage charged under the Additional Wage ceiling

description: Bonus keyed by HR; paid in full as keyed; Additional Wages for CPF.

references.title: Employment Act 1968 ss.10,11,23 — salary in lieu of notice is the gross salary for the unserved notice

description: Salary in lieu of notice keyed by HR; paid in full as keyed (EA ss.10, 11).

references.title: Employment Act 1968 s.45 — no statutory retrenchment benefit below 2 years’ service; longer service is contractual or negotiated

description: Retrenchment benefit keyed by HR; paid in full as keyed; not statutory below 2 years’ service (EA s.45).

references.title: Employment Act 1968 s.29 — recovery of actual loss after inquiry, limited to one quarter of a month’s salary

description: Deduction for proven damage or loss after inquiry, as keyed; at most a quarter of the month’s salary (EA s.29).

references.title: Employment Act 1968 s.30 — deduction for accommodation supplied and accepted, within its value

description: Deduction for accommodation supplied and accepted, as keyed, within its value (EA s.30).

references.title: Employment Act 1968 s.30 — deduction for amenities or services authorised by the Commissioner, within their value

description: Deduction for amenities or services authorised by the Commissioner, as keyed, within their value (EA s.30).

references.title: Employment Act 1968 ss.27(1)(j),32(1) — consented registered co-operative dues are outside the 50% deduction cap

description: Deduction of consented co-operative society dues, as keyed; outside the 50% deduction cap (EA ss.27(1)(j), 32).

references.title: Employment Act 1968 s.29(1) — the quarter-month limit may be exceeded with the Commissioner’s permission

description: Deduction for damage above the quarter-salary limit, as keyed, with the Commissioner’s permission (EA s.29(1)).

references.title: CPF Act 1953 First Schedule — wages for one month payable by the 14th of the next month are Ordinary Wages

description: Back pay keyed by HR; paid in full as keyed; Ordinary Wages for CPF.

references.title: CPF Act 1953 First Schedule — wages not meeting the Ordinary Wage timing test are Additional Wages

description: Back pay keyed by HR; paid in full as keyed; Additional Wages for CPF.

references.title: CPF Board, Applying for refund of CPF contributions — prior wage repayment and contribution refund are separate actions

description: Deduction of wages the employee repays for an earlier period, as keyed; the CPF refund is applied for separately.

references.title: Retirement and Re-employment Act 1993 s.7C; MOM, Re-employment — EAP of 3.5 months’ salary, minimum $6,250, maximum $14,750

description: Employment Assistance Payment keyed by HR when re-employment is not offered (3.5 months’ salary, $6,250 to $14,750; RRA s.7C); paid in full as keyed.

references.title: CPF Board, Who should receive CPF contributions — directors’ fees voted at a general meeting are not wages

description: Director’s fee voted at a general meeting; paid in full as keyed; not wages for CPF.

references.title: CPF Act 1953 s.7(3)–(4); CPF Board, Recovering the employee’s share — a missed employee CPF share may be recovered from later wages

description: Deduction recovering an employee CPF share missed earlier, as keyed (CPF Act s.7(3)–(4)).

references.title: Employment Act 1968 ss.10,11,23 — actual notice and unserved notice determine notice-pay liability

description: Deduction of the employee’s notice-pay liability for notice not served, as keyed (EA ss.10, 11).

references.title: Employment Act 1968 ss.27(1)(a),28(3) — a deduction for absence may recover the cost of food supplied during it

description: Deduction for food supplied during an absence, as keyed (EA ss.27(1)(a), 28(3)).

references.title: Employment Act 1968 s.27(1)(e),(i) — a deduction for amenities, services or another benefit requires the employee’s written consent

description: Deduction for a benefit the employee consented to in writing, as keyed (EA s.27(1)(e), (i)).

references.title: Income Tax Act 1947 s.45; IRAS — gross public-entertainer fees are subject to 15% withholding

description: Fee to a non-resident public entertainer; paid in full as keyed; 15% withheld (ITA s.45).

references.title: A statutory correction is an adhoc entry on this item. A year that comes out overpaid raises an obligation for the HR controller to enter it.

description: Tax or a contribution overpaid, paid back to the employee. The entry quantity is the refund; the statutory schemes are not re-run.
